exercises.objective: Explain why the LQR value function is itself a Lyapunov function for the closed-loop system.
exercises.prompt: DYN-04 gives the LQR value function $V(x,t)=x^\top P(t)x$. DYN-06 defines a Lyapunov function as any $V(x)$ proving stability. Explain why, for the steady-state (infinite-horizon) LQR case where $P$ is constant, $V(x)=x^\top Px$ is automatically a valid Lyapunov function for the closed-loop system $\dot x=(A-BK)x$.
hints: A Lyapunov function needs $V(x)>0$ for $x\ne0$ and $\dot V(x)<0$ along closed-loop trajectories. $V(x)=x^\top Px$ is positive definite whenever $P$ is (which it is, being a value function: cost-to-go can't be negative).

Since $P$ solves the algebraic Riccati equation, differentiating $V$ along the closed-loop dynamics gives $\dot V=x^\top(A-BK)^\top Px+x^\top P(A-BK)x$, which the Riccati equation's structure guarantees simplifies to $-x^\top(Q+K^\top RK)x$.

Since $Q$ and $R$ are the cost weighting matrices, chosen positive (semi)definite, $-x^\top(Q+K^\top RK)x\le0$: exactly the Lyapunov decrease condition. So the same $P$ that makes LQR optimal also directly certifies the closed loop's stability, no separate Lyapunov function needs to be found.

exercises.objective: Explain why controllability is necessary for a stabilizing LQR solution to exist.
exercises.prompt: Explain why $(A,B)$ being controllable (DYN-06's rank condition on the controllability matrix $C$) is necessary for the LQR gain $K$ to actually be able to stabilize the system, regardless of how the cost weights $Q,R$ are chosen.
hints: If $(A,B)$ is uncontrollable, some mode of the system (some eigenvalue direction) can't be influenced by the input $u$ at all, by definition of controllability.

If that uncontrollable mode happens to already be unstable (positive real-part eigenvalue) in the open-loop system, no choice of feedback gain $K=R^{-1}B^\top P$ can move it, since $u=-Kx$ can only act through directions $B$ reaches.

So controllability is necessary (though the weaker condition 'stabilizability', uncontrollable modes are all already stable, is technically sufficient) for LQR to find a stabilizing $K$ at all; no amount of tuning $Q,R$ fixes an uncontrollable unstable mode.

exercises.objective: Derive and numerically check the closed-loop stability of a linearized pendulum under PD control.
exercises.prompt: DYN-01 derives the pendulum's equation of motion $mL^2\ddot\theta+mgL\sin\theta=u$. Linearize around $\theta=0$, apply a PD control law $u=-K_p\theta-K_d\dot\theta$ (DYN-02), and derive the closed-loop state matrix $A$ (DYN-06). For $m=1,L=1,g=10,K_p=5,K_d=2$, compute the eigenvalues and classify stability.
hints: Linearizing $\sin\theta\approx\theta$ near $0$: $mL^2\ddot\theta\approx-mgL\theta+u$. Substituting $u=-K_p\theta-K_d\dot\theta$: $\ddot\theta=-\dfrac{mgL+K_p}{mL^2}\theta-\dfrac{K_d}{mL^2}\dot\theta$.
In state form $x=(\theta,\dot\theta)$: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-(mgL+K_p)/(mL^2)&-K_d/(mL^2)\end{pmatrix}$. With the given numbers, $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-15&-2\end{pmatrix}$.

Eigenvalues: $\lambda^2+2\lambda+15=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-1\pm i\sqrt{14}$. Real part $-1<0$: asymptotically stable (oscillatory-damped, per DYN-06's classification, since the eigenvalues are complex with negative real part). Independently verified numerically.

exercises.objective: Repeat the stability analysis with a sign-flipped derivative gain, showing instability.
exercises.prompt: Using the same linearized pendulum and $A$ matrix formula, now with $m=1,L=1,g=10,K_p=5,K_d=-1$ (a sign error on the derivative gain, a real and common implementation bug). Compute the eigenvalues and classify stability.
hints: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-15&1\end{pmatrix}$ (note the $+1$ in the bottom-right, from $-K_d/(mL^2)=-(-1)/1=1$).
Eigenvalues: $\lambda^2-\lambda+15=0\Rightarrow\lambda=0.5\pm i\sqrt{14.75}$.

Real part $+0.5>0$: unstable (growing oscillation). This is exactly why a sign error on the derivative gain is a dangerous, easy-to-make bug: the system doesn't fail to converge, it actively diverges. Independently verified numerically.

exercises.objective: Compute a controllability matrix and its rank.
exercises.prompt: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-2&-3\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}$, compute the controllability matrix $C=[B\ \ AB]$ and its rank. Enter the rank as a number.
hints: $AB=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-2&-3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\end{pmatrix}$.
$C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&-3\end{pmatrix}$.
$\det(C)=0\times(-3)-1\times1=-1\ne0$, so rank$(C)=2=n$: the system is controllable.

exercises.objective: Compute controllability for a system where it fails.
exercises.prompt: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$, $B=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix}$ (the input only directly affects the first state), compute the controllability matrix's rank. Enter a number.
hints: $AB=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix}$.
$C=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$: the second row is entirely zero.

rank$(C)=1<2=n$: NOT controllable. The second state ($x_2$, decoupled from $x_1$ with its own eigenvalue $2$) can never be influenced by $u$ at all, exactly what the zero second row of $C$ shows directly.

exercises.objective: Derive the error dynamics of inverse-dynamics tracking control and check their stability.
exercises.prompt: DYN-03's inverse-dynamics tracking law sets $\ddot q^*=\ddot q^\text{ref}+K_p(q^\text{ref}-q)+K_d(\dot q^\text{ref}-\dot q)$, then $u=M(q)\ddot q^*+F(q,\dot q)$. Assuming a perfect model (so the true $\ddot q=\ddot q^*$), derive the closed-loop dynamics of the tracking error $e:=q-q^\text{ref}$, and show they take exactly DYN-02's point-mass PD form, for ANY nonlinear robot. For a single joint with $K_p=9,K_d=6$, compute the error dynamics' eigenvalues and classify.
hints: Since $\ddot q=\ddot q^*=\ddot q^\text{ref}+K_p(q^\text{ref}-q)+K_d(\dot q^\text{ref}-\dot q)$, subtract $\ddot q^\text{ref}$ from both sides: $\ddot q-\ddot q^\text{ref}=-K_p(q-q^\text{ref})-K_d(\dot q-\dot q^\text{ref})$, i.e. $\ddot e=-K_pe-K_d\dot e$.

This is exactly DYN-02's point-mass PD closed-loop equation ($m\ddot q=-K_p(q-q^*)-K_d\dot q$, with $m=1$ here since inverse dynamics has already cancelled out $M(q)$ entirely) — the whole point of feedback linearization: however nonlinear the true robot dynamics $M(q),F(q,\dot q)$ are, the tracking error always obeys this same simple linear ODE.

In state form $\xi=(e,\dot e)$: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-K_p&-K_d\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-9&-6\end{pmatrix}$. Eigenvalues: $\lambda^2+6\lambda+9=(\lambda+3)^2=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-3$ (double root): critically damped, matching DYN-02's own condition $K_d^2=4K_p$ ($36=36$). Independently verified numerically.

exercises.objective: Repeat the error-dynamics stability check with underdamped gains.
exercises.prompt: Using the same error-dynamics state matrix, now with $K_p=25,K_d=4$. Compute the eigenvalues and classify.
hints: $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-25&-4\end{pmatrix}$.
Eigenvalues: $\lambda^2+4\lambda+25=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-2\pm i\sqrt{21}$.

Real part $-2<0$: asymptotically stable, but oscillatory-damped this time (complex eigenvalues), since $K_d^2=16<4K_p=100$: underdamped, per DYN-02's classification. Independently verified numerically.
